licences.notes: Words as printed in the Peters vocal score: Miei Signori, notajo, Vò, Don Alfonso's “eccola quà” (the libretto has Eccolo), coll' usata as two words, “È il contratto” (the libretto has E, and), giudiziarie (the libretto has giudicarie), legitima, soscriviam, quà.

licences.source: Edition Peters vocal score (Edition Peters Nr. 4474, plate 11446, edited by Georg Schünemann), pages 328–333, bars 204–289 of No. 31
licences.author: Kurt Soldan (1891–1946), piano reduction
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: the No. 31 Finale (671 bars) read in fourteen page ranges, sung lines and piano each by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the zoomed page by a judge, a separate sweep for dynamics and other marks, then checked bar by bar by eight fresh proofreaders (one fix in this section: the left-hand D♯ in bar 6 is a stemless whole note in a second voice). The German singing translation is left out. All the singers of this section have a staff throughout, with rests where the print leaves a staff out; singers who do not sing in this section are left out. Cut from the one-file finale at bars 204–289: from the first bar of the Allegro (also the last bar of “E nel tuo, nel mio bicchiero”: the words on its first beat belong to that section) to the bar before the Maestoso. In bar 86 the flute run of nine 32nds is a 9:8 group; its last note is 3 ticks longer than the others in the file, because 840 divisions cannot be split by 9, and the file's step back to the left hand was 3 ticks short of the bar, so it is set to the full bar (no note changed). Playback tempo ♩ = 186 (a half note = 93) from René Jacobs's recording (harmonia mundi), whose track for the canon and this scene lasts 3:43 (this section about 2 minutes).
